name: Settled Draw
description: Draw with the qi already full in the edge so the first cut of the exchange carries its whole weight.

name: Settled Ward
description: Sink the stance and hold the blade across the body with qi settled along it to take a heavy blow.

name: Through Step
description: Step through the target's reach on the line of the blade so the body passes the point of danger.

name: Edge Taper
description: Draw the qi on the edge down to the point and thrust so the whole force arrives on a finger's width.

name: Lasting Edge
description: Feed a steady thread of qi into the edge during the cut so every stroke of the exchange bites as deep as the first.

name: Qi Rebound
description: Take a blow on the flat and let the qi spring back along the edge into a counter cut.

name: Sundering Edge
description: Settle the whole body behind one stroke so the edge parts guard and bone together in a single heavy cut.

name: Unbroken Edgeward
description: Keep a living sheet of sword qi along the guard through a long exchange so each blow is met by fresh force.

name: Weighted Cut
description: Drop the weight of the body into a plain downward cut so the dense qi in the edge drives it deep.

name: Loaded Draw
description: Draw the sword with the hips behind it so the first stroke lands with a loaded edge and a firm base.

name: Rooted Edgeguard
description: Plant both feet and let the qi flow down the legs so a heavy blow on the blade cannot move the body.

name: Loaded Step
description: Advance a short step with the weight kept low so the blade stays loaded for the following stroke.

name: Falling Weight
description: Let the blade fall under its own weight onto the target's guard so the sword is driven down and the arm numbed.

name: Plumb Edge
description: Hang the blade straight down to catch a cut on the weighted edge and bring it back up in a cut of its own.

name: Weight Break
description: Bear down on the target's blade with dense qi until it sags and the guard opens for a cut.

name: Crushing Edge
description: Bring the full weight of the body and a dense core of qi down in one stroke that crushes a guard flat.

name: Dense Edge
description: Pack qi into the blade and the arm until the wielder's guard and cuts both gain a heavy lasting weight.

name: Extended Edge
description: Throw the qi out past the tip so the cut lands a hand's breadth beyond the length of the steel.

name: Outer Edge
description: Hold a thin rim of qi beyond the blade so a blow strikes the rim before it reaches the steel.

name: Edge Cast
description: Fling a crescent of qi from the edge that flies a dozen paces and cuts what it meets.

name: Reach Stride
description: Lengthen the stride behind the extended point so the body closes the gap the qi has already crossed.

name: Stretching Thrust
description: Push a needle of qi ahead of the point so the thrust pierces at twice the reach of the steel.

name: Long Edge
description: Stretch the blade with a bright line of qi and cut in a sweep that reaches a full pace beyond the steel.

name: Reaching Ward
description: Meet a blow well before it arrives with the outer edge of qi and turn it from the body.

name: Outer Blade Hold
description: Wrap the extended edge about the target's weapon from afar and hold it away from the body.

name: Beyond Edge
description: Gather qi for a breath then loose a great cut that carries the edge of the sword far beyond the steel.

name: Outstretched Guard
description: Spread a broad guard of sword qi well out from the body to stop blows long before they land.

name: Split Edge
description: Part the edge of qi in two at the moment of the cut so the stroke bites at two points.

name: Fan Cut
description: Spread the cut into a fan of three thin lines of qi that open the target from three sides.

name: Scattered Guard
description: Break one blow into many glancing touches with many small edges of qi so none of them lands fully.

name: Quick Edges
description: Cut four times in the space of one stroke with the qi dividing among the cuts.

name: Edge Volley
description: Throw a handful of thin edges of qi from one sweep of the blade at the target's chest and arms.

name: Multiplying Cut
description: Cut once and let the qi echo the stroke in a second and third edge that follow a heartbeat behind.

name: Edge Mirror
description: Raise many small edges of qi that turn a blow aside and send a returning edge back along its line.

name: Thousand Edges
description: Gather qi then loose a dense burst of fine edges that cuts every foe within reach of the sword.

name: Edge Corona
description: Spin a ring of fine edges around the body that shields the wielder and cuts any foe who presses close.

name: Twin Cut
description: Cut along two near lines in one motion so the second stroke follows the first before the target guards.

name: Paired Draw
description: Draw the sword and the scabbard together so a cut and a rap arrive at the same instant.

name: Dual Guard
description: Hold the blade and a bracing arm of qi side by side so a blow is met on two tracks.

name: Hawk Crouch
description: Drop and spring in a low hawk crouch to carry the body across the line of the blade.

name: Paired Edge
description: Cut with the edge while the flat of qi guards the same line so one motion both strikes and covers.

name: Twin Riposte
description: Turn a blow down one track and cut back along the other before the striker recovers.

name: Twin Track Cleave
description: Run body and blade down two tracks at once so the cleave comes from two angles and cannot be turned by one guard.

name: Azure Shell
description: Wrap the wielder in a pale blue shell of paired qi layers that takes blows on two tracks at once.

name: Stooping Swordcut
description: Drop from a high guard and cut downward in a steep stoop with the qi gathered at the edge.

name: Wingblade Cover
description: Throw both arms wide with the blade held out to form a spread guard of qi on either side.

name: Talon Thrust
description: Strike downward with the point curled like a talon to pierce at the shoulder or the neck.

name: Falling Bladestep
description: Drop from a spring onto the target's flank with the knees bent to absorb the fall.

name: Soaring Draw
description: Rise on the toes and draw upward in a high slanting cut that carries the body into the air.

name: Edge Plunge
description: Dive from a leap in a straight line to cut the target's shoulder and land beyond it.

name: Wing Ward
description: Sweep the blade up and out like a wing to turn a cut over the shoulder and away.

name: Claw Rake
description: Rake the point down the target's arm in three claws of qi that tear the grip loose.

name: Hawk Rend
description: Fall on the target from above with the whole weight of the body behind a single piercing talon of qi.

name: Pinionsteel Veil
description: Spread a veil of qi like a pinion behind the wielder as the body glides clear of a blow.

name: Left Edge
description: Cut from the left side with the first of two blades of qi so the stroke opens the target's guard.

name: Right Edge
description: Follow the left edge with a cut from the right so the pair closes on the target together.

name: Crossed Guard
description: Cross the two swords of qi before the chest so a heavy blow breaks upon the crossing.

name: Twinned Thrust
description: Thrust with both blades at once along parallel lines so the target cannot turn both aside.

name: Twinned Step
description: Glide forward with a blade out on each side so the two edges lead the body in.

name: Mirrored Draw
description: Draw both blades outward together in matching arcs that meet the target from either flank.

name: Crossing Cuts
description: Cut in a scissor of two arcs that cross at the target and seal off the line of retreat.

name: Scissor Edge
description: Close both edges on the target's blade like shears and snap it out of the grip.

name: Pair Ward
description: Catch a thrust between the two blades and turn it past the body in a single twisting motion.

name: Twofold Surge
description: Surge in behind both blades at once so two cuts land as the feet land.

name: Twin Sword Rend
description: Bring both swords of qi down together in one crushing rend that tears through a guard and what lies behind it.

name: Azure Cross
description: Hold the crossed azure blades as a living guard that cuts anything that presses on the crossing.

name: Heading Cut
description: Take a bearing on the target and cut along it with the edge held true to the line.

name: Sworn Steel
description: Hold the blade on a sworn line and let qi bind the guard to it so the line does not break.

name: Held Heading
description: Fix the blade on its bearing and breathe so the wielder's cuts keep to the line and gain in force.

name: Edge Heading
description: Advance step by step along the sworn bearing so the body never leaves the line of the point.

name: Oathsworn Edge
description: Cut with an edge sworn to the bearing so the stroke does not turn aside for a feint.

name: Oathblade Ward
description: Turn a blow along the sworn line and answer it with a cut that keeps to the same bearing.

name: Truing Edge
description: Read the bearing of the target's blade from one touch and cut at its true line.

name: Oath Rend
description: Cut along the sworn bearing with the whole oath behind the edge so the stroke tears through a guard.

name: Steadfast Bearing
description: Hold the sworn bearing unbroken so the guard stands against blows and the wielder's next cuts grow stronger.

name: Held Steel
description: Hold the edge on its line until the target moves into it then cut without any change of angle.

name: Level Heading
description: Keep the blade level on its bearing so a layer of qi spreads flat and takes a cut squarely.

name: Heading Thrust
description: Drive the point straight along the bearing so the thrust lands in the exact spot the line marked.

name: Edge Stride
description: Take a wide even step to hold the bearing while the target circles round the point.

name: Heading Draw
description: Draw the sword straight onto the held bearing so the first stroke is already on the line.

name: Bearing Mark
description: Mark the target's position with a thread of qi from the point and feel it shift.

name: Taut Bladeline
description: Hold a taut line of qi from the point so the target cannot step across the bearing.

name: Heading Strike
description: Cut along the held bearing and read from the contact how the target's weight has shifted.

name: Steady Swordheading
description: Hold the heading through a rush of steps and finish with a cut along the same bearing.

name: Unwavering Edge
description: Cut along the held bearing with an edge that does not waver for any feint and splits what it meets.

name: Fixed Heading
description: Fix the guard on its bearing with qi so every blow along the line meets a rooted shell.

name: Loose Blade
description: Hold the blade loose and low with no fixed guard and turn each cut aside as it comes.

name: Unbarred Edge
description: Cut from any line at all with no set stance so the edge cannot be read before it moves.

name: Bare Draw
description: Draw bare of any flourish in the plainest line so the cut leaves the sheath with no warning.

name: Blade Drift
description: Drift in a loose line around the target's reach so the feet make no clear approach.

name: Loose Thrust
description: Thrust from a slack wrist so the point arrives from no line the target expected.

name: Bare Ward
description: Leave the body open and raise a quick shell of qi only where the blow will land.

name: Unwalled Shell
description: Keep no fixed guard and let a shell of qi form wherever the blow is bound to fall.

name: Free Edge
description: Cut with the blade free of any set path so each stroke chooses its line in the moment.

name: Sworn Drift
description: Drift past the target's guard on a sworn line and cut as the body goes by.

name: Freeblade Reach
description: Reach round the target's blade with a loose cut that sets its guard spinning out of line.

name: Unwalled Rend
description: Cut free of any guard or stance with the full force of the open edge to rend the target's defense.

name: Free Heading
description: Move without a fixed line while a shell of qi follows the body and meets each blow as it comes.
